description: Drawing conclusions from samples with stated uncertainty: sampling distributions, estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, t-tests and ANOVA, chi-square tests for categorical data, linear regression with its assumptions checked, and non-parametric and resampling methods. Every procedure is first watched at work on thousands of simulated samples in the browser, then derived, then applied to real data such as district health records and market prices.
modelledOn: Wasserman, All of Statistics: A Concise Course in Statistical Inference
Rice, Mathematical Statistics and Data Analysis
Efron and Hastie, Computer Age Statistical Inference
outcomes: Derive and simulate the sampling distributions of common statistics and explain the role of the central limit theorem.
Construct point estimators by the method of moments and maximum likelihood and compare them by bias, variance and mean squared error.
Build and interpret confidence intervals and carry out hypothesis tests, reporting p-values, effect sizes and power correctly.
Compare groups with t-tests, ANOVA and chi-square tests and choose the right test for the design and data type.
Fit linear regression models, check their assumptions with diagnostics and draw valid inferences from the coefficients.
Apply non-parametric tests, the bootstrap and permutation tests when parametric assumptions fail.

units.title: Populations, samples and sampling distributions
topics: Populations, parameters, samples and statistics; simple random, stratified, cluster and systematic sampling; sampling frames and bias
Random variables refresher: expectation, variance, the normal, binomial, Poisson and exponential families
Sampling distribution of the mean and of a proportion; standard error; the law of large numbers
The central limit theorem stated, simulated and its limits with skewed data and small samples
Distributions derived from the normal: chi-square, Student's t and F; their shapes and degrees of freedom
Simulating thousands of household surveys in a Ghanaian district to watch estimates vary

units.title: Point estimation
topics: Estimators and estimates; bias, variance, mean squared error and consistency
Method of moments estimators
Maximum likelihood: the likelihood and log-likelihood, solving the score equation, numerical maximisation
Properties of maximum likelihood estimators: invariance, asymptotic normality, Fisher information and the Cramer-Rao bound
Sufficiency and efficiency in brief; Bayesian point estimates as a contrast

units.title: Interval estimation
topics: Confidence intervals: the pivotal method and what the confidence level does and does not mean
Intervals for a mean with known and unknown variance; intervals for a proportion (Wald, Wilson) and for a variance
Sample size calculation for a desired margin of error; finite population correction
Intervals for differences in means and proportions
Estimating malaria test positivity across district clinics with honest margins of error

units.title: Hypothesis testing
topics: Null and alternative hypotheses; test statistics, rejection regions and p-values; one- and two-sided tests
Type I and type II errors; significance level, power and power curves; sample size for a target power
The Neyman-Pearson lemma and likelihood ratio tests; the duality of tests and confidence intervals
Tests for a mean, a proportion and a variance; z and t tests
Multiple testing: family-wise error, Bonferroni and Holm corrections, false discovery rate with Benjamini-Hochberg
Misuse of p-values, p-hacking and the replication crisis; reporting effect sizes and intervals instead of only significance

units.title: Comparing groups: t-tests and ANOVA
topics: Two-sample t-test with pooled and Welch variances; paired t-test; checking normality and equal variance
One-way analysis of variance: partitioning sums of squares, the F statistic and the ANOVA table
Post hoc comparisons: Tukey's HSD and planned contrasts
Two-way ANOVA with interaction; randomised block designs
Effect sizes: Cohen's d and eta squared; basics of experimental design and randomisation
Comparing maize yields across fertiliser treatments in a field trial

units.title: Categorical data and chi-square tests
topics: Contingency tables; joint, marginal and conditional proportions
Chi-square goodness-of-fit test; expected counts and the small-count rule
Chi-square test of independence and test of homogeneity; standardised residuals
Fisher's exact test; McNemar's test for paired proportions
Measures of association: relative risk, odds ratio and their confidence intervals; Simpson's paradox

units.title: Linear regression and its assumptions
topics: Correlation and simple linear regression by least squares; the regression line and R squared
Inference for slope and intercept; confidence intervals for the mean response and prediction intervals
Multiple regression in matrix form; categorical predictors and interactions; the overall F test
Assumptions and diagnostics: linearity, independence, constant variance, normal errors; residual and Q-Q plots
Leverage, influence and Cook's distance; multicollinearity and variance inflation factors; transformations
Correlation versus causation; confounding and omitted variables
Modelling tomato prices at Kumasi Central Market against season, rainfall and transport cost

units.title: Non-parametric and resampling methods
topics: Rank-based tests: sign test, Wilcoxon signed-rank, Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis
Spearman's rank correlation; Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
The bootstrap: resampling, bootstrap standard errors, percentile and BCa confidence intervals
Permutation tests for group differences and correlation
When resampling fails: dependence, very small samples and extreme statistics

units.title: Inference in practice
topics: Choosing a method: a decision guide by question, design and data type
Frequentist and Bayesian inference compared: prior, posterior and credible intervals in brief
Survey data in practice: weights, non-response and design effects
Reproducible analysis and honest reporting; preregistration
Capstone: a full inferential analysis of a public Ghanaian dataset with a written report
